segments.html:
🖨️ Custom Product Printing

Place a custom or standard print order — cups, shirts, tabletop items, and more — then track its status from payment all the way through delivery. Once your design is ready you can view it right here, and after your order arrives you can leave us feedback.

New Order

Fill out the details below and we’ll get started on your order. You’ll get an email once it’s confirmed. Fields marked * are required.

Custom designs are generated using Canva’s AI design tools, which are subject to third-party usage limits. Design generation may occasionally be delayed if those limits are reached.

Use the format Street, City, ST ZIP — city before state, and no comma between the state and ZIP.
Paste publicly accessible image URLs. Each will be attached to the order record.

Track My Order

Enter the email address you used when placing your order — we’ll pull up all your orders and their current status.

parts.text:
Here's **Printing Business App**.

Want to change the app? Tell me how!

Want to use the app? Use the UI 👉, or ask me to!

Add a polished header section at the top of the main screen, above the tabs:
- A short, friendly title: "Custom Product Printing"
- A one-paragraph description: what this app does for the customer — place a custom or standard print order (cups, shirts, tabletop items, and more), track its status from payment through delivery, view your design once it's ready, and leave feedback after delivery.
- Below that, a clearly styled link/button (use the existing .arch-btn style) labeled "Print Shop staff? Open the Ops Dashboard →" that calls archestra.ui.openLink("PASTE_OPS_APP_URL_HERE") when clicked.

Keep it clean and not cluttered — this sits above the existing New Order / Track My Order tabs, doesn't replace them.
I'll help you add that header section. Let me first load the Build App skill and examine the current app code.
Now let me read the current app HTML to find where the tabs are.

I can see the current structure. There's already an `.app-header` block above the tabs. The user wants a polished header section with a new title, a longer description, and an Ops Dashboard button.

First, I need the Ops Dashboard URL. Let me find the "Print Shop Ops Dashboard" app.

The Ops Dashboard is `f333c6ea-aff0-4915-b81b-b0053e3de5d9`. Its standalone page path is `/a/print-shop-ops-dashboard`. Let me use the standalone URL for the openLink call.

Now let me update the header. I'll replace the existing `.app-header` styles and markup with a polished header section including the new title, description, and Ops Dashboard button.
I need to call it through `run_tool`.
Keys are `old_str`/`new_str`. Let me correct.
Now let me validate the app.

Done! I added a polished header section to the top of **[Printing Business App](/a/printing-business-app)**, above the New Order / Track My Order tabs (which are untouched):

- **Title:** "🖨️ Custom Product Printing"
- **Description:** one paragraph covering placing a custom or standard order (cups, shirts, tabletop items, and more), tracking status from payment through delivery, viewing your design once ready, and leaving feedback after delivery.
- **Button:** a ghost-styled `.arch-btn` labeled "Print Shop staff? Open the Ops Dashboard →" that opens the Ops Dashboard via `archestra.ui.openLink()`.

One note: you asked me to paste the Ops URL where `PASTE_OPS_APP_URL_HERE` was. I found your **Print Shop Ops Dashboard** app and wired the button to its standalone page, `/a/print-shop-ops-dashboard`, rather than a literal placeholder — so it works out of the box. If you'd rather it point somewhere else (a full external URL, for example), just give me the address and I'll swap it in.
I'll apply the background to the body and add the visual polish. Let me make these edits, targeting the customer-facing app (Printing Business App).
Now let me add a hover effect to the ghost header button (which uses `.arch-btn`, not the local `.btn-ghost` class) and the `.btn-link` links, then validate.

Done! The polish is live on **[Printing Business App](/a/printing-business-app)**:

- **Background** — the black wavy-line SVG pattern now covers the page body (fixed so it stays put while scrolling). Cards, form fields, and order cards keep their existing light backgrounds, so all text stays fully readable.
- **Card shadows** — the form/content card and each order card now have a `0 4px 20px rgba(0,0,0,0.4)` shadow so they lift off the dark background.
- **Button shadows** — primary submit buttons, the Pay Now button, the View Design/Video buttons, and the Ops Dashboard header button all carry the matching soft shadow.
- **Hover effects** — buttons rise slightly (`translateY(-1px)`) with a stronger shadow and a color shift, settling back on click; text links shift color on hover. All transitions are a quick, subtle ~180ms.

This was applied only to the customer-facing app, not the Ops Dashboard.
this the link for the OPS dashbaord, http://localhost:3000/a/print-shop-ops-dashboard
I'll update the Ops Dashboard button to use that full URL.
Done — the "Print Shop staff? Open the Ops Dashboard →" button on **[Printing Business App](/a/printing-business-app)** now opens `http://localhost:3000/a/print-shop-ops-dashboard`.

Fix the New Order form: Product and Color must be dropdowns, not free-text inputs, sourced from the Inventory table (tblug3ePb55apEEPK, fields: Product Name fldGrZPIWm5cyagka, Color fldIrWBRUbiljueJg).

- Product: a dropdown listing the distinct Product Names that exist in Inventory (no free text, no duplicates).
- Color: a dependent dropdown that only shows the Colors that actually exist in Inventory for whichever Product is currently selected — it should update its options whenever Product changes, and reset/clear its own selection if the previously selected color isn't valid for the new product.

This was working correctly before but has reverted to plain text inputs (visible in the current form) — likely overwritten by a recent styling change. Make sure the dropdown functionality survives alongside the current background/box-shadow/hover styling, not replaced by it.

The current HTML I read earlier already has `<select>` elements for Product and Color, with `loadInventory()` populating products and a `change` handler for the dependent color dropdown. Let me re-read the current state to see what's actually there now — the user reports they've reverted to text inputs.

The markup still has `<select>` elements, and `loadInventory()` populates products via a `change` handler for the dependent color dropdown. The reason it "reverts to plain text inputs" is the `catch` block: when the inventory load fails, it replaces the selects with text inputs as a fallback. 

The root cause: the code requests `fields: ['Product Name', 'Color']` by display name and reads `r.fields?.['Product Name']`. If the tool returns fields keyed differently (or the request fails), it silently degrades to text inputs. Let me preview the tool's actual output shape for the Inventory table to confirm the key format.

The tool works and returns fields keyed by display name (`"Product Name"`, `"Color"`), exactly what the code expects. So `loadInventory()` should succeed and build the dropdowns correctly.

The problem must be in the `catch` fallback triggering for another reason — most likely a JS error inside `loadInventory()`. Looking closely: the `.trim()` calls assume the field is a string. That's fine here. But there's a subtle bug — the fallback `catch` block replaces `f_product` and `f_color` selects with **text inputs**, and crucially, if *anything* throws (including the `change` listener being attached to an element that got replaced), it degrades. 

Actually the real issue: the user says it "reverted to plain text inputs." Since the tool clearly works now, the most robust fix is to **remove the text-input fallback entirely** so the fields are always dropdowns, and make the color dropdown properly reset its selection when the product changes. Let me also preserve the previously-selected color if still valid, and clear it otherwise.

Let me rewrite the inventory logic to be dropdown-only and robust, and improve the change handler.

Now the Reset button handler manually rebuilds the color select — let me update it to call `refreshColors()` instead, so it stays consistent (after `form.reset()`, product returns to its first option, so colors should reflect that).
The submit handler reads `$('f_product').value.trim()` and `$('f_color').value.trim()` — `.trim()` works on select `.value` too, so that's fine. Let me validate.

Fixed on **[Printing Business App](/a/printing-business-app)**. Product and Color are now guaranteed dropdowns:

- **Product** — a dropdown of the distinct Product Names from the Inventory table (no duplicates, alphabetically sorted). I verified the live data — it lists all 15 products (Ceramic Coffee Mug, Classic T-Shirt, Tabletop Plant, etc.).
- **Color** — a dependent dropdown that shows only the Colors that exist in Inventory for the selected Product, rebuilt every time Product changes. If the previously chosen color is still valid for the new product it's kept; otherwise it clears itself so a stale color can't be submitted.

The key fix for the "reverted to text inputs" problem: the old code had a fallback that **silently swapped the selects for free-text inputs** whenever the inventory load hit any snag. I removed that entirely — the fields now always stay dropdowns. On the rare load failure you instead get an error banner with a **Retry** link, and the Product select stays a select.

All of this lives alongside the background, box-shadow, and hover styling — none of that was touched.

Update the Shipping Address field on the New Order form: change the placeholder/hint text to show a concrete example in the format that actually works for shipping label creation — Street, City, ST ZIP:

"e.g. 4101 Church St, Retail Plaza, Apt 331, Chicago, WI 83378"

Keep it as helper/placeholder text under or inside the field, not a separate validation — just guidance so customers enter addresses in the right order (city before state, no comma between state and ZIP).
I'll update the Shipping Address field's placeholder and add a helper hint below it. Currently it's a textarea with `placeholder="Street, City, State, ZIP, Country"` and no hint.

Done on **[Printing Business App](/a/printing-business-app)**. The Shipping Address field now shows the example placeholder `e.g. 4101 Church St, Retail Plaza, Apt 331, Chicago, WI 83378`, plus a helper line beneath it: "Use the format **Street, City, ST ZIP** — city before state, and no comma between the state and ZIP." It's guidance only — no new validation was added.
add a small fill button on click it will automatically fill the 4101 Church St, Retail Plaza, Apt 331, Chicago, WI 83378 address, since its a hackthon during demo it would be nice to show

I'll add a small "Fill" button next to the Shipping Address field that populates the demo address on click. The diagnostics are a transient host-handshake timeout (SDK couldn't connect during that render), not a code bug — my change doesn't depend on it.

Done on **[Printing Business App](/a/printing-business-app)**. There's now a small "⚡ Fill sample" button on the Shipping Address label — one click drops in `4101 Church St, Retail Plaza, Apt 331, Chicago, WI 83378`, clears any error state, and focuses the field. Perfect for the demo.

A note on the diagnostics you saw: those were a one-off host handshake timeout — the app's SDK couldn't connect to the host within 10s during that render, so tool calls (loading products, etc.) would have stalled. It's an environment/connection hiccup, not a bug in the app code, and typically clears on a reload. If it keeps happening when you open the app, let me know and we can look into the host/bridge side.
Also for the reference Image URLs section add a fill as well and it will fill https://archestra.ai/logo.png
I'll add a matching "⚡ Fill sample" button to the Reference Image URLs field.

Done on **[Printing Business App](/a/printing-business-app)**. The Reference Image URLs field now has its own "⚡ Fill sample" button that drops in `https://archestra.ai/logo.png` on click. The live render also came back clean this time — the earlier handshake hiccup has cleared.

Update the Shipping Address field's placeholder/hint text on the New Order form — the current example has a geographic error (mismatched state/ZIP for Chicago) that could lead customers to enter invalid addresses that fail carrier validation later.

Replace the placeholder/hint with this corrected example:

"e.g. 4101 Church St, Retail Plaza, Apt 331, Chicago, IL 60601"

Same Street, City, ST ZIP order as before — just the corrected, real address values.
I'll update the placeholder and the "Fill sample" button to use the corrected address (Chicago, IL 60601).

Done on **[Printing Business App](/a/printing-business-app)**. The Shipping Address placeholder now reads `e.g. 4101 Church St, Retail Plaza, Apt 331, Chicago, IL 60601` (IL 60601 is a valid Chicago ZIP), and the "⚡ Fill sample" button fills the same corrected address. Format hint and everything else unchanged.

enhancement.description: Printing Business App — an interactive app built in chat.
enhancement.prompt: Build a customer-facing MCP App called "Custom Product Printing" for a print shop, backed by an Airtable base (Orders + Inventory tables), with two tabs: New Order and Track My Order. New Order tab: - Fields: Customer Name, Customer Email, Phone Number (with country code, required), Product (dropdown sourced from Inventory's distinct Product Names), Color (dependent dropdown — only shows colors that exist in Inventory for the currently selected Product, resets if the product changes), Quantity, Order Type (Standard or Custom Design), Shipping Address (multiline, with placeholder hint showing an example in "Street, City, ST ZIP" order, e.g. "4101 Church St, Retail Plaza, Apt 331, Chicago, IL 60601"), Description, Reference Images (URL paste, optional). - On submit, create a new record directly in the Orders table via the Airtable MCP server. Don't set Stage manually — that's handled by an Airtable automation that fires on record creation, notifying the shop and setting Stage to "New." - Show a visible disclaimer about Canva's AI design-generation usage limits somewhere on this tab. - Include a cross-app link/button ("Open the Ops Dashboard →") for staff, using archestra.ui.openLink() to the Ops Dashboard app's URL.
